messages:
Eli (AE): Quick heads up — Banyan POC (enterprise fintech) wants to test a custom Llama-derived model variant they trained: `banyan-13b-qlora-8bit`. They need hosted trial + optional private deploy. Security flagged KMS + VPC. Can infra/ML confirm catalog fit and any blockers?

Rina (SRE): What are the hard constraints? latency SLO, max batch, and peak QPS? Also need to know memory footprint for continuous batching.

Eli (AE): Customer targets 200 reqs/min with p95 latency < 250ms for short-chat (~256 tokens). Peak burst to 500 reqs/min for 10m windows. They expect KV-cache support for context window reuse.

Carlos (ML Eng): Quick read: `banyan-13b-qlora-8bit` likely fine but 8-bit qlora + custom tokenizer can break our optimized kernels (RMSNorm hotpath). I ran a local scan — found RMSNorm op alignment issues on cuBLAS path.

Carlos (ML Eng): Repro snippet:
```
redwood-cli model check --model banyan-13b-qlora-8bit --checks kv-cache,ops,rmsnorm
# output: rmsnorm_kernel_mismatch -> fallback to reference path (higher latency)
```

Rina (SRE): If RMSNorm falls back we may violate p95. Options: 1) we patch runtime kernel for RMSNorm (2-3d estimate), 2) recommend customer a 4-bit quant or different variant, 3) run on Dedicated with headroom and accept higher cost.

Maeve (Security): From compliance side: customer requires KMS-managed keys for model encryption and per-tenant audit logs. For private deploy they want HSM-backed KMS and VPC peering. Are there any data-paths that leak tokens to hosted logs?

Carlos (ML Eng): Hosted API currently stores minimal metadata; payloads are not logged unless debug is enabled. For private we can turn off telemetry and enable customer KMS/HSM. Need ticket to ensure model variant artifacts are stored in customer-controlled S3 for Private.

Eli (AE): Pricing ask from procurement: rough monthly for a 2-week POC (hosted) with reserved burst capacity and an estimate for Dedicated node sizing (for procurement hold). Can we give a ballpark?

Rina (SRE): Ballpark hosted trial cost (token compute + burst): ~$6k for 2 weeks at 200->500 reqs/min with 256 tokens average (assumes 13B 8-bit). Dedicated (single 80GB A100 equiv pool + autoscale buffer): ~$25k/mo booked, min 1-month commitment. (very rough)

Carlos (ML Eng): Technical recommendation: For POC use hosted but pin to variant with KV-cache disabled initially to avoid extra memory pressure. If they need prefix caching, enable on Dedicated only. If we patch RMSNorm kernel fast, we can enable KV-cache hosted.

Maeve (Security): Action items for sec: 1) Provide customer with SOC2 artifact list, 2) draft KMS integration plan for private deploy, 3) confirm audit log retention options. I can take 1 & 2.

Eli (AE): Timeline suggestion: This week — run compatibility scan + estimate patch effort. Next week — share POC pricing and security checklist with customer. Can Rina/Carlos own the scan?

Rina (SRE): I'll run full infra compatibility run tomorrow against `banyan-13b-qlora-8bit` and post results. Will include memory profile for batching.

Carlos (ML Eng): I'll try a quick kernel patch PoC. If I can reproduce easily, I can open a runtime PR; ETA 48–72h.

DeployBot: Canary deploy scheduled for branch `rlib/rmsnorm-fallback-fix` to staging at 2024-06-21T03:00:00Z — monitor latency dashboards.

Eli (AE): Awesome. I'll draft the customer reply after we get the scan. Small ask: can we give procurement a not-to-exceed hosted estimate they can use for internal approval?

Rina (SRE): Use $8k as NTE hosted (includes buffer). I'll attach the detailed memory/batch numbers when the scan finishes.

Maeve (Security): I'll attach the SOC2 checklist and a short KMS plan by EOD tomorrow.

Eli (AE): Thanks team — looping in customer after Rina's scan + Maeve's docs. :thumbsup:
